name_note: GTDB places Gardnerella inside the genus Bifidobacterium, so this taxon appears as s__Bifidobacterium greenwoodii, while the literature name is Gardnerella greenwoodii.

sentences.text: Gardnerella greenwoodii was proposed as a novel species of the genus Gardnerella, based on a strain isolated during a female urinary microbiome study from the urine of a healthy postmenopausal woman.
Its 16S rRNA gene sequence placed it in the genus Gardnerella, and its highest average nucleotide identity was with Gardnerella swidsinskii.
Gardnerella species have been described as key drivers of bacterial vaginosis, a condition reported to affect nearly one in three women of reproductive age.
A genomic analysis of Gardnerella isolates resolved 21 genomic lineages encompassing 11 species and 15 subspecies, with lineage-specific repertoires of virulence and metabolic genes.
